children.proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be fixed, and define F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. We prove that F_n(x+z) = F_n(x) for every real x and every integer z.

Since z is an integer, for any real t we have floor(t+z) = floor(t) + z. Applying this with t = nx and t = kx gives

floor(n(x+z)) = floor(nx+nz) = floor(nx) + nz,

and for each k = 1, ..., n,

floor(k(x+z)) = floor(kx+kz) = floor(kx) + kz.

Therefore

sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k = sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+kz)/k
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + sum_{k=1}^n z
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz.

Substituting into the definition of F_n gives

F_n(x+z) = floor(n(x+z)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k
= (floor(nx)+nz) - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz)
= floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= F_n(x).

Hence F_n is periodic with period 1, so the stated identity holds for all real x and all integers z.

Fix n>1 and an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1. Let x,y be real numbers such that m/n<=x<=y<(m+1)/n. Then m<=nx<=ny<m+1, so floor(nx)=floor(ny)=m. Also, for each k=1,2,...,n, since x<=y and k>0 we have kx<=ky, hence floor(kx)<=floor(ky). Therefore
F_n(x)-F_n(y) = (floor(nx)-floor(ny)) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)-floor(ky))/k
= sum_{k=1}^n (floor(ky)-floor(kx))/k >= 0,
because each summand is nonnegative and each k is positive. Thus F_n(x)>=F_n(y), so F_n is nonincreasing on [m/n,(m+1)/n).

Fix an integer n > 1 and an integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1. By the definition of F_n, for any real x,

Substitute x = m/n. Then

F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k m/n)/k,

which is exactly the desired identity.

children.proof_nl:
Let F(m) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k, where 0 <= m <= n-1.

For each k, write km = n*q_k + r_k with 0 <= r_k < n. Then q_k = floor(km/n), so
floor(km/n)/k = m/n - r_k/(nk).
Summing over k = 1,...,n gives
sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k = m - (1/n) sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k,
so
F(m) = (1/n) sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k.
Thus we only need to maximize sum r_k/k.

Now let d = gcd(m,n), and write n = dN, m = dM with gcd(M,N) = 1. Because multiplication by M permutes the residues modulo N, the multiset {r_k : 1 <= k <= n} consists of d copies of each multiple
0, d, 2d, ..., (N-1)d.
Let a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n be these residues in nonincreasing order. Since the weights 1/k are strictly decreasing, swapping any inversion increases the sum; hence the largest possible value of sum r_k/k is attained when the residues are arranged in nonincreasing order. Therefore
sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k <= sum_{k=1}^n a_k/k.

The sorted list is explicit: each value n-d, n-2d, ..., 0 appears exactly d times, so
 a_k = n - d*ceil(k/d).
In particular, d*ceil(k/d) >= k, so a_k <= n-k for every k. Hence
sum_{k=1}^n a_k/k <= sum_{k=1}^n (n-k)/k = n*H_n - n,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k. Combining this with F(m) = (1/n) sum r_k/k gives
F(m) <= H_n - 1.

It remains to check equality. If d > 1, then a_1 = n-d < n-1, so the inequality a_k <= n-k is already strict at k = 1, and thus F(m) < H_n - 1. Therefore equality can occur only when d = 1.

If d = 1, then the residues r_k are a permutation of 0,1,...,n-1. The swap argument is then strict unless the sequence is already nonincreasing, so equality forces
r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_n.
A nonincreasing permutation of 0,1,...,n-1 must be n-1, n-2, ..., 0. Thus r_1 = m = n-1. Conversely, when m = n-1, we have floor(k(n-1)/n) = k-1 for k < n and floor(n(n-1)/n) = n-1, so
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(n-1)/n)/k = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k + (n-1)/n = n - H_n,
which gives F(n-1) = H_n - 1.

Therefore, for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1,
m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k <= H_n - 1,
with equality if and only if m = n-1.

Let x = m + t, where m = floor(x) ∈ Z and t = frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1).
For each k ∈ {1,2,\dots,n}, since km is an integer we have
floor(kx) = floor(km + kt) = km + floor(kt).
Now t < 1 implies kt < k, so floor(kt) ≤ k-1. Also t ≥ (n-1)/n and k ≤ n, hence
kt ≥ k(n-1)/n = k - k/n ≥ k-1,
so floor(kt) ≥ k-1. Therefore floor(kt) = k-1 for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Thus, for every such k,
floor(kx) = km + k - 1,
and in particular floor(nx) = nm + n - 1.
Substituting into the definition of F_n(x),
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - \sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n (km+k-1)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(m + 1 - 1/k\bigr)
= (nm+n-1) - (nm + n - H_n)
= H_n - 1,
where H_n = \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Hence whenever frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1), we have F_n(x) = H_n - 1.

so floor(kt) ≥ k-1. Therefore floor(kt) = k-1 for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Thus, for every such k,
floor(kx) = km + k - 1,
and in particular floor(nx) = nm + n - 1.
Substituting into the definition of F_n(x),
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - \sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n (km+k-1)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(m + 1 - 1/k\bigr)
= (nm+n-1) - (nm + n - H_n)
= H_n - 1,
where H_n = \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Hence whenever frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1), we have F_n(x) = H_n - 1.

Therefore the maximum is H_n - 1 and the maximizers are exactly the integers translates of that last interval, equivalently the real x with frac(x) in [(n-1)/n,1).

Recursive lemma proofs:

1. lem_20260329003149_d2ff8f59: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. Then for every real x and every integer z, F_n(x + z) = F_n(x).
Let n > 1 be fixed, and define F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k. We prove that F_n(x+z) = F_n(x) for every real x and every integer z.

Since z is an integer, for any real t we have floor(t+z) = floor(t) + z. Applying this with t = nx and t = kx gives

floor(n(x+z)) = floor(nx+nz) = floor(nx) + nz,

and for each k = 1, ..., n,

floor(k(x+z)) = floor(kx+kz) = floor(kx) + kz.

Therefore

sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k = sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)+kz)/k
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + sum_{k=1}^n z
= sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz.

Substituting into the definition of F_n gives

F_n(x+z) = floor(n(x+z)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+z))/k
= (floor(nx)+nz) - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nz)
= floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= F_n(x).

Hence F_n is periodic with period 1, so the stated identity holds for all real x and all integers z.

2. lem_20260329003154_5ae9f7ea: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For any integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1 and any real numbers x,y satisfying m/n <= x <= y < (m+1)/n, one has F_n(x) >= F_n(y).
Fix n>1 and an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1. Let x,y be real numbers such that m/n<=x<=y<(m+1)/n. Then m<=nx<=ny<m+1, so floor(nx)=floor(ny)=m. Also, for each k=1,2,...,n, since x<=y and k>0 we have kx<=ky, hence floor(kx)<=floor(ky). Therefore
F_n(x)-F_n(y) = (floor(nx)-floor(ny)) - sum_{k=1}^n (floor(kx)-floor(ky))/k
= sum_{k=1}^n (floor(ky)-floor(kx))/k >= 0,
because each summand is nonnegative and each k is positive. Thus F_n(x)>=F_n(y), so F_n is nonincreasing on [m/n,(m+1)/n).

3. lem_20260329003200_cd20d473: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k m/n)/k.
Fix an integer n > 1 and an integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1. By the definition of F_n, for any real x,

F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k x)/k.

Substitute x = m/n. Then

F_n(m/n) = floor(n(m/n)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k.

Since n(m/n) = m and m is an integer, floor(n(m/n)) = floor(m) = m. Therefore

F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k m/n)/k,

which is exactly the desired identity.

4. lem_20260329003209_47690510: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define H_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, m - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k m/n)/k <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if m = n-1.
Let F(m) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k, where 0 <= m <= n-1.

For each k, write km = n*q_k + r_k with 0 <= r_k < n. Then q_k = floor(km/n), so
floor(km/n)/k = m/n - r_k/(nk).
Summing over k = 1,...,n gives
sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k = m - (1/n) sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k,
so
F(m) = (1/n) sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k.
Thus we only need to maximize sum r_k/k.

Now let d = gcd(m,n), and write n = dN, m = dM with gcd(M,N) = 1. Because multiplication by M permutes the residues modulo N, the multiset {r_k : 1 <= k <= n} consists of d copies of each multiple
0, d, 2d, ..., (N-1)d.
Let a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n be these residues in nonincreasing order. Since the weights 1/k are strictly decreasing, swapping any inversion increases the sum; hence the largest possible value of sum r_k/k is attained when the residues are arranged in nonincreasing order. Therefore
sum_{k=1}^n r_k/k <= sum_{k=1}^n a_k/k.

The sorted list is explicit: each value n-d, n-2d, ..., 0 appears exactly d times, so
 a_k = n - d*ceil(k/d).
In particular, d*ceil(k/d) >= k, so a_k <= n-k for every k. Hence
sum_{k=1}^n a_k/k <= sum_{k=1}^n (n-k)/k = n*H_n - n,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k. Combining this with F(m) = (1/n) sum r_k/k gives
F(m) <= H_n - 1.

It remains to check equality. If d > 1, then a_1 = n-d < n-1, so the inequality a_k <= n-k is already strict at k = 1, and thus F(m) < H_n - 1. Therefore equality can occur only when d = 1.

If d = 1, then the residues r_k are a permutation of 0,1,...,n-1. The swap argument is then strict unless the sequence is already nonincreasing, so equality forces
r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_n.
A nonincreasing permutation of 0,1,...,n-1 must be n-1, n-2, ..., 0. Thus r_1 = m = n-1. Conversely, when m = n-1, we have floor(k(n-1)/n) = k-1 for k < n and floor(n(n-1)/n) = n-1, so
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(n-1)/n)/k = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k + (n-1)/n = n - H_n,
which gives F(n-1) = H_n - 1.

Therefore, for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1,
m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k <= H_n - 1,
with equality if and only if m = n-1.

5. lem_20260329003216_0cb7f112: Let n be an integer greater than 1, define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k, and define frac(x) = x - floor(x). If frac(x) lies in the interval [(n-1)/n, 1), then F_n(x) = H_n - 1, where H_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k.
Let x = m + t, where m = floor(x) ∈ Z and t = frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1).
For each k ∈ {1,2,\dots,n}, since km is an integer we have
floor(kx) = floor(km + kt) = km + floor(kt).
Now t < 1 implies kt < k, so floor(kt) ≤ k-1. Also t ≥ (n-1)/n and k ≤ n, hence
kt ≥ k(n-1)/n = k - k/n ≥ k-1,
so floor(kt) ≥ k-1. Therefore floor(kt) = k-1 for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Thus, for every such k,
floor(kx) = km + k - 1,
and in particular floor(nx) = nm + n - 1.
Substituting into the definition of F_n(x),
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - \sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n (km+k-1)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(m + 1 - 1/k\bigr)
= (nm+n-1) - (nm + n - H_n)
= H_n - 1,
where H_n = \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Hence whenever frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1), we have F_n(x) = H_n - 1.
